name: Banh canh Trang Bang
summary: Trảng Bàng’s other bowl: long, soft rice-flour strands made without tapioca, in a pork-bone broth simmered for hours until it runs sweet and deep. It comes with pork hock, lean pork, blood cake or fish cake, scallion, and pepper.
origin: Trảng Bàng, Tây Ninh. The bowl dates to the early twentieth century, when it was sold from shoulder poles on the road between Sài Gòn and Tây Ninh.
texture: The strands are milled from non-glutinous rice, partly cooked, then pressed into boiling water, so they stay off-white, soft, and firm in the hot broth and smell of rice.
taste: The broth is sweet and deep from the pork bones. Greens come on the side, and the meat is dipped in plain fish sauce pounded with fresh chili.
howToEat: Stop for a bowl in phường Trảng Bàng or along Quốc lộ 22, on the drive between Ho Chi Minh City and the Holy See or Ba Den.
The rooms fill on weekends, holidays, and in the high season.
where: Phường Trảng Bàng and Quốc lộ 22. Khu phố Gia Huỳnh serves it beside the rice-paper rolls.
seoTitle: Banh canh Trang Bang — the rice-flour bowl
seoDescription: Rice-flour bánh canh in a sweet pork-bone broth with hock, lean pork, and blood cake or fish cake, at the Trảng Bàng stop.
